STEP 2 - Vessel: The plate is a square dinner plate, roughly 26 cm across. Treating it as a square with an inner usable area gives roughly 26 × 26 ≈ 676 cm²; I'll use about 600 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Scrambled eggs (cooked with a little butter or oil) are the only visible food.

STEP 4 - Area: The scrambled eggs cover about 13% of the plate, which is about 78 cm². That 13% is also the total share of the plate covered by food.

STEP 5 - Volume: 78 cm² × 1.5 cm height = 117 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: The curds are fluffy and loose, so I use a bulk density of about 0.6 rather than the 0.9–1.0 for dense egg. 117 ml × 0.6 ≈ 70 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Scrambled eggs are about 150 kcal/100 g. 70 g × 1.5 ≈ 105 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 70 g is roughly 1.5 eggs, which is plausible for this small pile.
